status: independently witness-validated local exact classification; plantri/Actions reproduction pending
scope: Candidate 489 degree-12 dual-vertex substitutions with at most four inserted disk vertices, corresponding to primal orders 100, 102, 104, and 106.

method.structural_basis: The disk plus the removed apex is an even plane triangulation and therefore has a proper three-coloring. Boundary colors alternate. Color-class degree sums and rainbow-triangle constraints reduce k<=4 to finitely many polygonal decomposition types.
method.generation: Exact parity-first polygonal enumeration, quotienting by boundary dihedral symmetry and internal-vertex permutations.
method.reduced_filter: Closed dual is even and has vertex connectivity at least four.
method.hamiltonicity: Exact perfect-matching complement recursion with early closed-subcycle pruning.
method.positive_policy: Every positive stores an explicit selected-edge Hamiltonian-cycle witness, subsequently revalidated for edge membership, uniqueness, cardinality n, degree two, and connectedness.
method.negative_policy: No negative occurred. A negative would remain provisional until independent primal and dual proof encodings and checked DRAT/LRAT.

k4: three color-0 plus one boundary-colored vertex

families.interpretation: The unique disk is the original 12-wheel; all 89,402 raw neighbor-set/pocket constructions reduce to this class under the parity filter.
No parity-valid disk contains the edge between the two internal vertices. Both classes are boundary-chord-separated unions of one-center pieces.

limitations: The parity-first structural enumeration has not yet been independently reproduced by plantri because GitHub Actions remained queue-blocked.
The result is complete relative to the stated three-color structural derivation; it is not a classification of all Barnette graphs through order 106.
No non-Hamiltonicity proof was required because every reduced closure had an explicit cycle.
next_target: k=5 dual disks, corresponding to primal order 108, prioritized by color-class degree constraints and internal-edge structure.
